subject: Biology
title: Immunodeficiency: When Defenses Fail
description: Learn Immunodeficiency: When Defenses Fail in one minute.

hook.text: A child born without a working immune system must live in a sterile bubble—any germ could be fatal.

buildup.text: Primary immunodeficiencies are genetic. Secondary ones are acquired—like HIV destroying T cells.

discovery.text: SCID—severe combined immunodeficiency—leaves patients with no T or B cells at all.

twist.text: Gene therapy has cured some SCID patients by inserting a working copy of the defective gene.

climax.text: Bone marrow transplants can rebuild an immune system entirely by replacing defective stem cells.

punchline.text: No defense means any infection is a death sentence.

quiz.question: What is SCID?
options: A genetic disorder with no functional T or B cells
A type of allergy to all foods

details.summary: Immunodeficiency disorders weaken or disable parts of the immune system, leaving the body vulnerable to infections that healthy immune systems easily handle. Primary immunodeficiencies are inherited, while secondary types like AIDS are acquired through infection or treatment.
details.whyItMatters: Immunodeficiency reveals how critical each immune component is by showing what goes wrong without it. HIV/AIDS has killed over 40 million people, and understanding immunodeficiency guides treatments from antibody replacement to stem cell transplants.
takeaways: Primary immunodeficiencies are genetic; secondary types are acquired
HIV destroys helper T cells, collapsing coordinated immune defense
Treatment ranges from antibody infusions to bone marrow transplants

faq.question: How does HIV cause immunodeficiency?
faq.answer: HIV specifically infects and destroys CD4 helper T cells, which coordinate the entire adaptive immune response. As these cells decline over years, the immune system loses its ability to organize effective responses, leaving the body vulnerable to opportunistic infections and cancers.

faq.question: What was the bubble boy disease?
faq.answer: Severe Combined Immunodeficiency, or SCID, is a genetic disorder where both B and T cells are absent or nonfunctional. Without treatment, affected children cannot fight any infections and must live in sterile environments. Gene therapy and bone marrow transplants can now cure some forms.
